summary: Project Lodestar is a first-person space exploration game that introduces young people to spacecraft engineering and mission design. Players diagnose station failures, complete hands-on repairs, configure a communications CubeSat and plan an orbital rescue. Drawing on NASA’s CubeSat 101 guide and GMAT mission-design concepts, Lodestar connects scientific learning with meaningful gameplay. Players learn through decisions, consequences and opportunities to try again.
details:
Project Lodestar places players aboard a spacecraft where maintaining essential systems becomes part of a rescue mission. Players explore the station in first person, inspect equipment with a scanner and complete interactive repairs. Tasks involve manipulating components directly, helping connect scientific explanations with practical actions.

After receiving a damaged distress transmission, players configure and deploy a communications CubeSat to recover information from a stranded astronaut. They then use an orbital-planning interface to evaluate a rescue plan. NASA resources inform the satellite-design and mission-planning activities, while the fictional setting makes these concepts approachable.

Our educational approach follows a decision–consequence–feedback loop. Players encounter problems, investigate their causes, attempt solutions and receive feedback. The goal is to encourage curiosity about engineering and space exploration through active participation.

The browser-based game uses JavaScript, HTML, CSS and Three.js, with Blender and Python used to create 3D environments, models and animations. Claude and ChatGPT supported development and design, and Piper generated in-game voices.

Lodestar is an educational prototype intended for students and space-curious players. Its fictional missions and simplified systems support learning rather than professional astronaut training.
